title: Alabama AI Laws

reading.body:
Alabama has passed two AI-related laws, and neither one regulates AI as a technology. One governs how health insurers use it, the other creates a commission to study it.

The pattern is narrow and sectoral. SB63 targets a single use case, artificial intelligence in medical necessity determinations for prior authorization, and constrains it with process requirements: individualized clinical review, annual certification, a human clinician making the final call on denials, disclosure, periodic review, and data protections, with the Department of Insurance able to investigate and discipline. HJR51 does not regulate anything. It creates a commission on AI and children's internet safety, asks it to study effects and other states' approaches, requires a report to the Legislature by November 1, 2026, and then dissolves it.

For AI specifically, this is the shape most state activity takes before any broad statute exists. The binding constraint SB63 addresses is not compute or power but decision authority: who is accountable when a model's output determines whether care is covered. That is a question about human review and liability, and Alabama answers it by requiring a clinician in the loop rather than by limiting the model.

What this does not tell the reader is how either law performs in practice. There is no enforcement record, no data on how many determinations are affected, and no indication of whether the study commission's recommendations become legislation. Two laws is also a small base, and the page covers only what this site judged relevant to AI, so adjacent rules that touch automated decisions without naming AI would not appear here.

Alabama has enacted 2 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Alabama

2 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • SB63: Health care plans; to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in determinations of coverage passed 2026-04-17

    This Alabama law limits how health benefit plan providers may use artificial intelligence to make medical necessity determinations for prior authorization requests. It requires individualized clinical review, annual certification, human clinician final decisions on denials, disclosure, periodic review, and data protections. The Department of Insurance may investigate and discipline violations.

  • HJR51: Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety Study Commission, created passed 2026-03-10

    Creates the Study Commission on Artificial Intelligence and Children's Internet Safety to study the effects of artificial intelligence, social media, and Internet access on children, investigate other states' approaches, and develop recommendations for potential legislation. The commission must report to the Legislature by November 1, 2026, and then dissolves.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Alabama. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
